title: Обед для группы и ставка на Катю  (Lunch for the Crew and a Bet Over Katya)

segments.t: After Barinov ruins Take Three by calling Nagiyev's character a bone-breaker instead of a bonesetter, the crew breaks for lunch—while outside, Nikita and Denis bet their right to court Katya on the football game.
А кто я по сценарию?
Ладно, сейчас обед, немножко перекусите.
Все нормально, просто выучи текст, да?
Давай, иди учи слова.
Слушай, скучно так просто играть.
Может, нам ставку сделать, на деньги сыграть?
Но откуда у тебя деньги, давай так.
Если выиграешь ты, я вам с Катей больше не мешаю.
А если выиграю я, то уходишь ты.
Ты и так нам с Катей не помешаешь.
Ну что, согласен?
Давай, по рукам!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
А кто я по сценарию?

'And who am I in the script?' Over the work and the court, Nagiyev presses Denis for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Ладно, сейчас обед, немножко перекусите.
'Fine, it is lunch now, have a little bite.' Explaining that fine it is lunch now have a little bite lays the cards on the table for Denis.
Все нормально, просто выучи текст, да?

'Everything is fine, just learn the lines, okay?' Asking whether everything is fine just learn the lines okay puts Denis right on the defensive. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Давай, иди учи слова.
'Go on, go learn the words.' Going on go learn the words moves the conversation forward without extra drama. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".
Слушай, скучно так просто играть.
'Listen, it is boring to play just like this.' Pointing out that it is boring to play just like this gives Denis a sobering reality check.
Может, нам ставку сделать, на деньги сыграть?

'Maybe we should make a bet and play for money?' Asking whether maybe they should make a bet and play for money puts Denis right on the defensive. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Но откуда у тебя деньги, давай так.

'But where would you get money, let's do it this way.' Realizing that where would Denis gets money let them do it this way changes how Nikita handles the situation. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
Если выиграешь ты, я вам с Катей больше не мешаю.
'If you win, I will not get in the way of you and Katya anymore.' Noting that if Denis wins he will not get in the way of Denis and Katya anymore keeps Nikita's side of the story simple and clear.
А если выиграю я, то уходишь ты.

'And if I win, then you walk away.' Even though if he wins then Denis walks away, Nikita keeps a steady face in front of Denis. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Ты и так нам с Катей не помешаешь.

'You will not get in the way of Katya and me anyway.' Admitting that Nagiyev will not get in the way of Katya and him anyway shows Denis being honest for a change. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
Ну что, согласен?
'Well, do you agree?' Asking whether Denis agrees cuts straight through the tension between Nikita and Denis.
Давай, по рукам!

'Let's do it, deal!' Declaring that they should do it deal brings Denis's temper right to the surface. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this". Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
А кто я по сценарию?
Ладно, сейчас обед, немножко перекусите.
Все нормально, просто выучи текст, да?
Давай, иди учи слова.
Слушай, скучно так просто играть.
Может, нам ставку сделать, на деньги сыграть?
Но откуда у тебя деньги, давай так.
Если выиграешь ты, я вам с Катей больше не мешаю.
А если выиграю я, то уходишь ты.
Ты и так нам с Катей не помешаешь.
Ну что, согласен?
Давай, по рукам!
With Katya's heart on the line, the second half of the courtyard football game turns fiercely competitive. See you next time!
До встречи!
